content.thinking:
I'm planning the proportions for a whimsical capybara with a bird perched on its head, working out body dimensions and a coordinate system with the capybara lying horizontal and facing forward.

Building the skeleton hierarchy...

Defining tail and leg chains...

Adding toes as small spheres at each foot's tip joint with toe-colored material, then planning the body as a loft through hips, spine, and neck stations along a smooth path.

I'm defining station widths and heights from rump to shoulders to get a realistic capybara profile, checking that leg attachment heights line up with the belly line, and setting up countershaded fur coloring with mottling for the body surface.

Now I'm defining the fur colors and layering a countershade and mottle paint through a cel-shading function, then moving on to building the blocky head shape with a loft from skull to the boxy muzzle.

Still writing head geometry...

Positioning the eye decals on the head surface using local offsets—placing them high and slightly back for that capybara look, with mirrored placement on each side and appropriate decal size and direction.

For the ears, I'm adding small flattened spheres scaled to look rounded on top-back of the head, with a smaller pink inner-ear part nested inside, using local offsets to position them correctly relative to the head.

Now I'm adding a whimsical little bird perched on top of the head—a small sphere body scaled slightly oblong, with its own joint hierarchy for a bird head, beak, tail, and wings, all parented to a joint sitting just above the head's crown.

Still detailing bird features...

Working out the bird's perch position on the head, checking that the head loft stations line up so the bird sits naturally on top without clipping—adjusting its body and head joint coordinates until the bottom of the bird body meets the head's top surface correctly.

Now I'm adding facial details: a few thin whisker rods per side extending from the muzzle, plus a small mouth line rod across the muzzle underside, positioning them carefully relative to the head bone.

Then I'm working on the lower jaw as a frustum box, figuring out its y-position and height so it sits correctly inside the bottom of the head volume without clipping.

I'm sketching small teeth boxes near the front, debating whether to risk placing cream-colored buck teeth near the nose area or skip them since they might get hidden by the nose pad. Now I'm considering fur tufts on the body, which would need card geometry and SVG textures.

Writing fur tuft code...

Then I'm brainstorming whimsical extras like a tiny scarf or flower accent, maybe a grass tuft or blossom near the feet, though I'm leaning toward skipping the ground base for now.

Adding a small daisy accent...

Now I'm working on belly countershading and darker toe tones. For the toes, I'm placing three small spheres per leg near the foot tip, sized and positioned to sit just at ground contact, checking the math so the rounded cap of the leg doesn't sink too far below the floor.

For the hind legs I'm making them chunkier with a larger thigh radius, repositioning the limb root and foot points, and setting up the knee bend direction for a natural forward-folding joint.

Now I'm figuring out the chain naming for each limb's spans and tip joints, assigning side roles, and determining which spine joint each limb attaches to based on proximity - front legs parenting to a spine joint, hind legs to the hips. I'm also checking the rig's side constraint requiring positive x-coordinates, and working out the bone hierarchy ordering from tail through hips, spine, neck, and head.

For overlapping joint positions like hips and spine1 sharing the same point, I'm resolving which span claims ownership by keeping the later-listed one, and confirming the tail chain doesn't interfere with the main loft path. Now I'm adding the tail stub chain with its joint coordinates.

Writing sweep and fur edge code...

Still layering shading logic...

I'm adding whimsical touches like blush cheeks and small feather details while keeping the part count modest, staying careful to only import what's actually used.

Now I'm scattering fur cards across the body surface with tinted colors, skipping toon outlines, and wiring up decals for the eyes against the head sweep surface before finalizing the build function.

Working through the limb chain signature, foot tip placement, whisker rods, joint aim options, and jaw box coloring...

For the bird I'm figuring out the belly shading with countershading paint, placing the eye sphere, and working out crest spikes positioned along the head with upward-angled directions for each of the three spikes.

For the legs I'm keeping things simple with tiny orange rods and a small foot sphere since most of this is hidden anyway, and I'm wrapping up by placing the ears relative to the head using local left/up/forward offsets, computing their final position.

Now I'm adding a small flower decoration near the ear, built from a ring of petal spheres around a yellow center, positioned just behind the ear on one side.
